The UF Research Computing Center sits in Gainesville, Florida, operated by the University of Florida. No power capacity or IT load is published for this facility. The operator's own spec pages, which this site uses as its only source for capacity figures, contain no megawatt rating for this campus.

This facility appears designed to serve internal university research and campus computing needs rather than external commercial tenants or hyperscale AI workloads. The research status is exhausted, meaning available public sources do not describe the facility's current specifications, age, or power infrastructure in the terms required to assess its role in AI scaling.

Florida has 13 mapped data center facilities, of which only 4 operators publish power figures, totaling 9.35 MW statewide. This campus ranks fifth among Florida facilities by published megawatts, which means it is not among the four that have disclosed capacity to this site. Without published specifications, this campus cannot be ranked against the state's commercial AI infrastructure.
